note: Everything below (angles, seeds, pixel sizes, deposition, thresholds, stopping rule) is fixed HERE, before the first production run of this round. Nothing may be tuned after inspecting results; a change of estimator needs a new round with a new prereg.

object_under_test.role: production shear-band inclination measurement of CASE-BIAXIAL-SHEAR-BAND (scatter-point Radon / projection focus, eta2 criterion, equal-count bins)
object_under_test.note: the anchor name radon_projection_measurement denotes this measurement operator; it is the only place where a band inclination is read out of a particle field in this repository

reference_implementation.construction: pad to square of the diagonal (circle=False), rotate about the image centre with the source's exact 3x3 matrix R via a spline warp, sum axis 0 -> one projection per angle
reference_implementation.local_substitution: skimage C extensions are binary-incompatible with the installed numpy (ValueError: numpy.dtype size changed), so skimage.transform.warp cannot be imported; the same R is applied with scipy.ndimage.affine_transform(order=1). Equivalence is asserted in tests/test_radon_reference.py against closed-form sinograms (centred delta, disc) and the known angle convention.
reference_implementation.measurement_criterion: projection focus on the sinogram; primary = normalised-projection energy sum(p_hat^2); sensitivity = minimum entropy / peak / raw variance. The transform is OSS, the focus criterion is the classical projection-focus family (same family as our eta2, law of total variance)

decision.question: Does TensorDEM's scatter-point radon_band_angle agree with the mature OSS image-domain Radon projection measurement on fields of known inclination, within the owner 15% accuracy standard, and can the OSS route replace or feed back into ours?
alternatives: A: keep the scatter-point estimator unchanged (no interpolation, no raster, angle-independent cost); OSS used only as an external check
B: replace the scatter-point estimator by the OSS raster+rotate+sum route (needs an isotropic grid and a deposition kernel; introduces splat + spline smoothing)
C: keep A but import OSS boundary-condition lessons (isotropic sampling, scale-free focus criterion, deposition-width rule)
decision.predeclared_choice_rule: adopt C by default; adopt B only if the OSS route is at least as accurate on every group AND cheaper; adopt A-with-defect-fix if the XVAL exposes a defect in ours that the OSS route does not have.

hypothesis.H1: on the case lattice (24x48 spacings, aspect sqrt(3)) and a ridge width of 2 spacings, both estimators recover the injected inclination within 15% relative error at pixel_size <= 0.5 spacings
hypothesis.H2: the two routes agree with each other within 15% (the anchor criterion)
hypothesis.H3: the OSS route needs a deposition kernel >= 1 particle spacing and pixel_size <= 0.25 spacings; below that it aliases onto the triangular-lattice directions and fails (>15%)
hypothesis.H0_falsifier: either estimator or their agreement exceeds 15% relative error on the primary group

metrics.primary: relative error of the recovered inclination: |theta_got - theta_true| / theta_true
metrics.secondary: absolute error in degrees; per-criterion angles of the reference; convergence of the error with pixel_size and with deposition width; angular-resolution sensitivity

acceptance.basis: owner accuracy standard (error > 15% unacceptable); 3% = report-level target

case_matrix.control_lattice: 32x32 (square in physical units), isolates lattice aspect as a confounder
case_matrix.production_field: finite-width tangential slip band imposed on the lattice (synthetic_band_configuration, slip 4% of height, width 3 spacings), weights = local_shear_strain (k=8) — i.e. the exact strain field measure_band projects

reference_settings.deposition: isotropic Gaussian, sigma = deposit_sigma_spacings * measured particle spacing, truncate 4

repetitions.primary: 3 independent lattice-jitter seeds per (angle, pixel_size) cell; all other groups are deterministic functions of the seed kept fixed, so they are single-run by design
repetitions.rationale: the only stochastic input is the jitter realisation; the estimator itself has no random component (no sampling, no initialisation). Repeating the sweeps would duplicate identical arithmetic.

exclusions.rule: a case is excluded only if an estimator raises or returns a non-finite angle; the exclusion count and reason must be reported, and >5% exclusions invalidate the round

stopping_rule: run the whole frozen matrix once; no threshold, seed, angle or pixel-size may be changed afterwards. If the anchor criterion fails, the round is an honest FAIL with the failing group reported.

environment.compute: cluster loong64 node (2 nodes, 128 cores each), one shard per process, no GPU

analysis.aggregation: per group and per (angle, pixel_size) cell: max and mean absolute/relative error; no averaging across groups
analysis.uncertainty: spread over the 3 seeds reported as min/max of the per-cell error
analysis.outliers: none removed; the aliasing cases of the deposit sweep are kept and reported as the failure mode they are
analysis.comparison: absolute and relative error against the injected (known) inclination; agreement between the two estimators on the identical weight field

interpretation_limits: synthetic weight fields and synthetic slip bands only: no run of the DEM case is repeated here, so nothing is claimed about the physics of a real biaxial test
the reference measures a *field*, ours measures a *point cloud*; agreement on the same weights does not prove both are unbiased for an arbitrary field
the OSS transform is reproduced from source with one documented substitution (scipy affine_transform for skimage warp) because the local skimage binary is broken
relative error uses the injected angle as denominator, so the same absolute error is penalised less at 80 deg than at 30 deg; absolute degrees are reported next to it
